Consider the arc of the curve $y=-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-4x$ that lies in the fourth quadrant between its $x$-intercepts. What integral gives the area of the surface generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis?

activity_context.topic_title: Surface Areas of Revolution: Rotation About the Y-Axis

feedback.problem: Consider the arc of the curve $x=\sqrt{y-3}$ that lies between the lines $y=3$ and $y=\frac{15}{4}.$ Calculate the surface area generated when this arc is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
We can find the surface area generated when a curve is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $y$-axis using the formula

$$
S=\int 2\pi x\,\text{d}s.
$$

Since we're given a curve in the form $x=f(y),$ we have 

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, we will use

$$
S=2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Computing the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(\sqrt{y-3})=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{y-3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}=\frac{1}{4(y-3)}.
$$

Then, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =2\pi {\int }_{{y}_{1}}^{{y}_{2}}x\sqrt{1+{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{3}^{15/4}\sqrt{y-3}\cdot \sqrt{1+\frac{1}{4(y-3)}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{3}^{15/4}\sqrt{y-3}\cdot \sqrt{\frac{4y-11}{4(y-3)}}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{3}^{15/4}\sqrt{4y-11}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

We evaluate the last integral using the substitution $u=4y-11.$ Then, $\text{d}y=\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.$

We also need to compute new limits:

| **$y$** | $3$ | $\frac{15}{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}S & =\pi {\int }_{3}^{15/4}\sqrt{4y-11}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}{\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\pi }{4}\cdot {[\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{{u}^{3}}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}(\sqrt{{4}^{3}}-\sqrt{{1}^{3}}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{6}(8-1) \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$
